stem: Bilal packs a pair of bar magnets for the science cupboard. He has a wooden strip, soft iron pieces, hard steel pieces, and soft rubber pieces. He must avoid heating, dropping, or hammering the magnets, and keep them away from a mobile phone on the shelf.

parts.text: Which storage choice keeps the magnets safer?

options.text: Unlike poles on the same side, wood between the magnets, and soft iron pieces across the ends.
Unlike poles on the same side, wood between the magnets, and hard steel pieces across the ends.
Unlike poles on the same side, soft iron across the ends, and the magnets touching with no wood.
Unlike poles on the same side, wood between the magnets, and soft rubber pieces across the ends.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Bar magnets should be stored in pairs with unlike poles on the same side, a piece of wood between them, and soft iron keepers across the ends.

teacher.key_rationale: Safe storage uses unlike poles on the same side, wood between the pair, and soft iron keepers. Hard steel or soft rubber are wrong end pieces, and omitting the wood is unsafe storage.
